answer: An agent marketplace called jetty requires each identity to lock $100 for 30 days before receiving a daily quota of ten bids. Quotas scale with locked funds, so splitting one deposit across fake identities creates no extra capacity. To add a delta of 1,000 daily bids, an attacker must lock $10,000 across 100 accounts. This makes a sybil spiral costly in tied-up capital, even if every deposit is eventually returned.
